title: Wring a wet sponge into a basin and return it to its rack
instruction: Hold both ends of the wet sponge over the basin and wring water into it. Return the sponge to the rack.
context: A wet cleaning sponge is wrung before storage. The arms need opposing grips on a flexible body while keeping the runoff inside the basin.
setup: A soft cellulose utility sponge about 152 by 91 by 24 mm, holding 90 g of water, lies across two drying-rack bars centred at X 448, Y 0 mm. An empty 198 by 284 by 44 mm basin is centred at X 295, Y 0 mm.
scoring: Score 0 for above 5 g spilled outside the basin or below 20 g caught. Score 0.25 when 20 g or more are caught, and 0.5 at 40 g or more. Score 1.0 if at least 40 g are caught and the sponge is released on its rack.
reset_notes: Rinse and squeeze the sponge by hand, then add water until it holds 90 g above its dry reference mass. Empty the basin and clear the catch surface before setting the wet sponge flat on its rack.
fidelity: Native torsional joints in three graspable sponge sections transmit resistance to both wrists. Runoff increases under counter-twist. After relaxation, further wringing draws from the reduced water reserve. The foam model omits individual pores, capillary forces and local pressure.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; stock YAM scripted demo: 1.0
